utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Black.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. I have about ten more minutes of redirect, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Black.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: We are back for another week but you won't be there the whole time, of course. Where we left off on Friday we were discussing some documents that related to Skabrnja, do you remember that general topic?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: I'd like you to look at another document now which is 65 ter number 1266, if this could be brought up on the screen. Mr. Theunens, this is cited at footnote 334 of your report and I would, for the Court officers' information I believe there is a problem on e-court. The easiest way to retrieve this English version is L 0064363. There's just problem in the connection between the translation and the original document. We are currently seeing the B/C/S version on the monitor. It would be helpful if we could have the English, please. Mr. Theunens, which version do you see on the monitor in front of you? Is that in English or B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have the English version in front of me, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I don't but that may well be my problem. Mr. Theunens, what is this document, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, what is this document?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours it says a statement of facts and I believe that we started to discuss this document on Friday already. I don't have the cover page in front of me so I don't know who took this statement. But based on what I wrote in my report it has to be a statement taken by Major Branislav Ristic or Lieutenant commander Simo Rosic about events in Skabrnja, i.e., the alleged crimes that were committed in Skabrnja.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And if you could look at the first paragraph of that statement of facts, just tell us specifically the subject of this document, please.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The author describes or writes that he conducted an interview of a JNA soldier, a private, whose name is Dragan Mitrovic and his duties consisted of driving a BOV which is an armoured combat vehicle. It's actually in -- an armoured personnel carrier. It looks a bit like a van but then on four wheels, no windows, and it's used by the infantry among others. And so Mitrovic, he took part in the combat operations in Skabrnja and he witnessed also the killings of civilians by members of the Territorial Defence and that has to be Territorial Defence of the SAO Krajina and volunteers. And then further on, the author provides the account of the events as they were witnessed by Dragan Mitrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Could you just read out or perhaps if it's easier to summarise the last couple of sentences of that paragraph which begin, "As we entered the village."

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There it states that when they --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milovancevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Defence has objection, Your Honour. This question shows us that the Prosecution raises an issue that wasn't part of this expert report. The subject of the expert report was the Territorial Defence and army of the Serbian Krajina, including the relevant documents which pertain either to the armed forces of the SFRY and the JNA or to the Territorial Defence of Krajina. I believe that by putting such questions, the Prosecutor goes beyond the expert report, as does the witness in answering such a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Black?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This document was cited in the expert report. As the witness just noted, it deals specifically with Territorial Defence units, and the reason I'm going into it now on redirect, Your Honour, is that on cross-examination, Skabrnja was dealt with and the thrust of council's questions were to focus on Croatian armed forces and, I would submit, an attempt to portray this as a regular armed conflict maybe with collateral damage et cetera. So my point on redirect is to go back and deal with Skabrnja in a little bit of detail as was cited and provided in the report to make sure the record is clear on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And you say this was already -- always part of the expert report.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour it was cited in footnote 334 of the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And you said it is 65 ter 1226 -- 66.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: 1266, correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. The objection is overruled. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, if you remember the question, I'd asked you to read or summarise beginning where it says, as we entered the village?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. I remember the question. It states that territorials and volunteers and some of them called themselves Chetniks, they brought a group of 20 civilians from a cellar and one of these -- one of them but I don't know whether the "them" refers to the civilians or to the volunteers and TO, had a PAP and a PAP is an acronym for a semi-automatic rifle. And apparently when you look further into the document it's obvious that the "them" refers to one of the civilians. So this civilian with the semi-automatic rifle, he was taken behind the armed personnel carrier and shot. And subsequently an old woman and an old man, they were lined in front of the armed personnel carrier, they had to lie on the ground and then they were shot in the back of their head.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And the next paragraph, please, could you just continue?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There, it's more of the same, so two other -- three men were taken from a house, it's not specified what these men were doing or who they were. They were questioned for a bit and then they were shot. And then the witness, this JNA private who participated in the operations, also stated in the interview that he had heard stories that they - and that -- the "they" refers to the volunteers and the TO, members - killed a woman of 19 and an 18-month-old child but he didn't -- he emphasised that he didn't see it himself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: : Sorry is that 8 or 18?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 18, excuse me. Sorry, 8 month, 8 month, I have an 8-month-old child.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And if we could turn to page 2 of this document briefly, please. The next page, if we could look at that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: There is a paragraph which begins, Mr. Theunens, "I saw territorials steering a group," could you please tell us what's dealt with in that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This indicates that according to the private, members of the Territorial Defence used local civilians as a human shield, so put them in front of the vehicle in order to facilitate the advance. Then, according to the witness, he says that the chief of the SJB so the Public Security Service which it is actually the police, SAO Krajina Police, Drazic, spoke to a captured civilian and then the witness mentions that he -- according to the information he heard, this civilian was also killed by the territorials or Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour could this document receive a number and be admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence and may it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit number 118, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I'd now like to ask you to look at Exhibit 107, which was shown to you during the cross-examination. If that could be put on the screen, please. Mr. Theunens, this is -- what you see, of course, is the English translation but of some handwritten notes by Lieutenant Colonel Bogunovic. Do you remember seeing this document in cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I remember seeing this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And specifically, if we could scroll down just briefly to the bottom of that first page, Mr. Theunens, you were asked questions about Ustashas and ammunition that had been captured. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: If we could turn now to page 3 of the English translation, Mr. Theunens, you'll see near the middle of the page it talks about 20 November 1991, analysis of the mop-up operation. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: If we could scroll down just a little bit more on the document, just above where it says page 19, there are a number of bullet points. Could you read the last two bullet points, please, Mr. Theunens?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says, "Arsons and looting, less than in some of early operations" and the second of the last bullet says "there were cases of uncivilised killings."

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: If we could turn to the next page of the English translation, please? Under the heading Zoran Lekic, if we could scroll down a bit, Mr. Theunens, could you tell us what's identified in the third bullet point, please?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The third bullet point says, "Three civilians were transported from the point 16 and killed in" the next word is illegible, and then it says, "Needs to be investigated."

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And three bullet points down from that there is a bullet point that begins the OB. What is said there?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There it says, Your Honours, the OB, which is the B/C/S acronym for security organ or security officer should take steps to identify those who committed crimes, robberies, and barbarities.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Could we please turn to the next page of the English version? Mr. Theunens, if you look under the heading Lieutenant Tadic, beginning with the second bullet point, could you just look through that list of bullet points and tell me if there is anything of note?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there is a reference first to people wearing Chetnik insignia and it also says that they cannot be used for further operations, a Cedo KV he tried to stop the killing but then they, and I assume that the "they" refers to the same people who were wearing the Chetnik insignia wanted to kill him. Then there is also further on a mention of a "he," he kills a man as soon as he sees him. He kills dogs. And then at the end there is a reference that some soldiers in the company started looting.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: If you could look down at the next group of bullet points after where it says, page 22, there is a bullet point that says "more than 20 killed." And what's that in the next bullet point?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There it says, Your Honours, they were about to kill a woman and a child saying Ustasha bastards.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: If you could go down slightly further on the page under the 2nd Lieutenant, if you could look at the fifth line about POWs, what does it say there?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: POWs were beaten to death.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Just so it's clear, what is POW an abbreviation for?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: POW stands for prisoners of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: If we could look briefly at the next page, please, where it says, 2nd Motorised Brigade, what's mentioned in the first bullet point there?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says that five to six conscripts, chronic alcoholics, they are a loose cannon and they should be removed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And finally can we look at the next page in the English, please? Mr. Theunens, if you'll look down the page a little bit as we scroll down, under where it says, it 10 December 1991, could you please read out the third and last bullet point?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The third bullet point, Your Honour, says, in Skabrnja, TO members killed one elderly person each day. And that refers to 10th of December 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: That's -- I've finished now with document -- Exhibit 107, and the last topic could we see Exhibit 109, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, do you remember seeing this document during your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do remember seeing that document, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And if we could please scroll down a bit. Thank you. Mr. Theunens, what is addressed in paragraph 3? What's said there?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this was the report by Lieutenant Ernest Radjen who was a military police officer and he describes the things he saw when he at one moment in time entered Skabrnja. In bullet 3 or point 3 he says that in the yard of a private house he found a man aged around 65, civilian, two women aged around 65, 70, in the cellar of the house, three elderly people and when we look at the beginning of the document these people have all been killed during the operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And where was this?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is in -- this is in Skabrnja, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Could we look at the second page, please, of the English translation? Mr. Theunens, I won't ask you of course to read out all the different paragraphs of this document but could you look at paragraphs 5, 6, 7, and 8 and tell us what's being addressed in these paragraphs?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, all these paragraphs mention people that have been killed during the operation in Skabrnja and the details who these people are. Most of these people are elderly, at least they are above 50, and it includes both men and women, and in some cases it explains not how the people were killed but Radjen makes an assessment on use of mortars, use of tanks, and provides additional information.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Does the document refer to the status of these dead people as being combatants or non-combatants in any way in any of the entries?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I remember well, and we can see that, for example, in bullet 9, Radjen makes assessments and he concludes that young men must have been ZNG members, so combatants. Now, for the others he states civilians and if I remember the document well, most of the people killed and described in Radjen's report are civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. And we have looked at a few paragraphs. Do other paragraphs in this document contain similar information?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, I think from paragraph 1 to 11 it's always the report talks about killed people, most of them civilians, and then at the end, paragraph 12 he Radjen talks about the presence of military equipment in the garage and then further on he talks again about victims, mainly civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Could we look at the last page, please? The last paragraph, in fact. What's addressed there, Mr. Theunens?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Radjen there states that according to his observations, no signs of violence or mutilation were noticed on the bodies except nor one body, where -- of a man who was wearing a ZNG uniform, whose right ear had been cut off.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Theunens. Your Honour, I have no more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Black.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, at page 640, line 25, 25, rather, counsel for the OTP, Mr. Black, asked how being a member of the OTP affected your analysis, either in the analytical process or in the reports you prepare, and you gave the system that you employed. Counsel for the Defence went to the issue of your integrity in the compilation of the report and your conclusions at the end of the day. Having regard to the fact that your brief is from the office of the OTP and your focus is, as contained in their brief, you've been an officer or a member of that department, how did this affect your treatment in -- of your work in compiling the report, in respect of collection, your analysis and your findings in the report or conclusions at the end of the day? And as to how you treated the parties herein.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, it is correct that I'm a member of the OTP. Now, when asked this question by Mr. Black, I explained the intelligence cycle to explain actually in order to make clear how intelligence analysis is being done. And actually, the only steering or the only guidance, if I can explain it like that, is done in the beginning by -- in the direction phase. So I received my tasking for drafting this report from a senior trial attorney who works for the Office of the Prosecutor and that was Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff and she told me in quite general terms that she wanted to have a report on the military structures in the entity known as the SAO Krajina and later the RSK and the relation between these structures and Milan Martic. Now, with this tasking I first drafted a table of contents of issues I believed or topics I believed that were relevant for that purpose and I showed that to Mr. -- excuse me, to Mrs. Uertz-Retzlaff and that must have happened sometime I think before summer 2004 or at the end of summer 2004. I was lucky that I had drafted already the report for the Milosevic case and that much of the background material I could take from the Milosevic case. So that was the direction. Secondly, of course, I went to collect information and it is correct that I only consulted the databases as they are in use in the Office of the Prosecutor. But, of course, the databases and the evidence available to the Office of the Prosecutor covers a very wide area of topics. It's not only evidence against one party because, of course, my colleague, I have a colleague who writes a report about Croatian Operation Storm, for example, he will look for information in the same database. In addition, I was very lucky that I could participate in document search missions in Croatia and there, of course, we have no guarantees that the Croatian authorities who had seized the documentation during the military operations in 1995 kept all the information they seized in the records and gave it to us. It may well be that they have selected certain material from there. That's something we have to accept. But again that was not really a problem because during the collection process, the information that was selected again based on the purpose of the report, it was obvious there was also Rule 68 material that I came across material that addressed crimes committed by other parties. I came also across material that included detailed information on the Croatian military operations between 1991 and 1995, and if it was Rule 68 then it was disclosed. If it was information that was, let's say, relevant for a colleague much mine who would draft a report on the Croatian operations I gave it to him. So then I drafted the report, I started my analysis, keeping in mind the tasking. It's not a conflict analysis. It is an analysis of the organisation, role, structure of one party in a conflict as well as the relations between this party and one individual, Milan Martic. I think a first draft was finalised sometimes in fall 2004. That was then sent to Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff and she only had some comments on the layout and, of course, spelling and issues like that but at no moment in time did I get any guidance from somebody in the Office of the Prosecutor or somewhere else that I had to write that Martic did this or Martic did that. It came from the documents and, I mean, it's up to you of course, Your Honours, to judge the value of the document and to see whether it answers the requirements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: Yes, but I wanted to ask you directly, having regard to cross-examination, would you, in compilation of the report, have exercised prejudice or preference against any party in the compilation of your report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would certainly not exercise prejudice or preference because that would affect the credibility of the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Theunens. My next question is: Bearing in mind the constitution and the laws of the defence in relation to the Minister of Interior and the Minister of Defence or those ministries, would there have been a conflict of interest in terms of both of those ministries residing in one person, in the operations concerning the army and warfare? Or in any other way that's material to your report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe you are referring to the situation that existed in the entity known as the SAO Krajina from early August or even end of July 1991 onwards until the end of 1991. My conclusion is that a distinction needs to be made between the de jure situation, i.e., as it is specified in the law, the laws you have mentioned, as well as the constitution, on one hand, and on the other hand the de facto situation. When we look at the documentation that's available for that time period and more specifically the number of decisions that are being taken by Milan Babic and the number of laws that are being issued, one gets the impression but I admit that is more a political analysis which is not really the subject of my report but, for what it's worth, one gets the impression that the situation is not 100 per cent clear, i.e., that Babic tries to impose his authority and therefore tries to rely on laws and decision, i.e., on de jure measures in order to confirm or impose his authority. There is a section in my report which starts at the bottom of page 95, in the English version, which talks about or the title is, "The power struggle between Milan Babic and Milan Martic." I have used that title because from the documents I came across that described the de facto situation, i.e., the situation as it is on the ground basing myself on reports of operations we had on specific orders, there, one sees that there could well be a conflict of interest and that even if Milan Martic was a ministry -- was Minister of Interior, that he also issued orders to the Territorial Defence. And that gives the impression that there is a difference between the de jure and a de facto situation, at least during the latter half of 1991, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Were the Territorial Defence not de jure under the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Territorial Defence according to the documents I reviewed, they were part of the SAO Krajina armed forces and they were subordinated to the president of the SAO Krajina. That's the de jure situation. And if I can find the exact reference, this is, for example, discussed on page number 90, where we discussed the decision by the SAO Krajina government on the 1st of August 1991, to adopt a law of defence of the Republic of Serbia, and in that decision, there is also a reference to the armed forces, in Article 6 of that decision. It says that the president of the government of the SAO -- of the Serb autonomous region of Krajina is by his position commander of Territorial Defence, i.e., armed forces of the Serb autonomous region of Krajina. The only question that could be raised but I think that should be raised by the person who took the decision or by a legal expert, is that in the 1st of August 1991 decision, there is a difference between the wording of paragraph 5, where the armed forces are defined, and it says it's the armed forces consist of the Territorial Defence and the police, and then in Article 6, when the authority of the president of the government is established, there, it says he's commander of the Territorial Defence, i.e., armed forces. There is no explicit mention made in Article 6 of the 1st of August 1991 decision to the police or the forces of the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: There is just one last question, and that has to do with the international laws of war which you spoke to, touching and concerning the manoeuvres of war and how persons, civilians, property, et cetera, were to be dealt with in the act of warfare or threat of war. What I want to know is this: Can one act outside of the laws of war, lawfully and, if yes, under what circumstances? For example, when can the commander or deputy commander or somebody in charge of a unit of troops go outside of the laws of war? And I'd also like to relate it, for want of a better word, to the foot soldiers on the ground. Could they go outside of the laws of war, international laws of war, properly?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm not aware of any circumstances where people, either soldiers or officers, can go outside of the international laws of war. I remember that there is, of course, a stipulation for protected facilities, that certain facilities have to be protected but then if these facilities are misused by the other party for military purposes then again this is being dealt with by the international laws and customs of war and they say that under those circumstances, a protected facility will lose its protection but it's -- there is a whole range of articles that deal with it. But again, that's why we have international laws of war. It is to cover each eventuality or each situation that can arise during a conflict. So there cannot be any justification for not abiding by these laws.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: And there is no discretion given to a person or an officer confronted with circumstances on the ground that would be permissible for him to act in a manner contrary to international laws of war, then?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm not a legal expert but from my training and education, I have never learned that as an officer, there were circumstances where I would be allowed to judge myself whether I should abide by the laws or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: That's what I wanted to know. I'm very grateful to you. Thank you, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, can I just ask one question? What is the difference between RSK and Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, these are -- the names used for two Serb -- two different Serb entities that were declared as a result -- or I wouldn't say as a result but during the conflict. RSK refers to the Republic of Serbian Krajina which is a continuation of the SAO of the Serb autonomous district of Krajina. Serb autonomous district of Krajina was declared end of 1990 and also the people who declared that entity decided that or, yeah, decided about the area, the territory that would be covered by this SAO Krajina, territory within the Republic of Croatia. At the end of 1991, the decision is adopted to transform the SAO Krajina into an RSK which means that also Serb-declared territories in Western Slavonia and Baranja, Eastern Slavonia would join and that, just if you could call it unification, was formalised in April 1992. So this covers the RSK. On the other hand, Republika Srpska the Bosnian Serbs, I believe it was in the course of end of April 1992 or at least before the 12th of May 1992, they declared their Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina in Bosnia-Herzegovina and this became later known under the acronym RS Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Theunens. There was a document, the last document that Mr. Black dealt with in his re-examination. I don't think it was admitted or anything was done to it. Do you want anything done to it, Mr. Black?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll be corrected by the Court officer if I'm wrong but I believe that was Exhibit 109 which had already been admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Any questions arising from the questions from the Bench? Mr. Black?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Not from the Prosecution, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have no questions. However, I would like Exhibit 711 from the OTP 65 ter list to be tendered as a Defence Exhibit. I don't know if I've done so already. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Milovancevic. Yes, we sort of had it in mind that we should ask about that. Document Exhibit 65 ter number 711, it will be admitted into evidence as a Defence Exhibit and may be given an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit number 119, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Milovancevic. That's it. Thank you very much, Mr. Theunens. Thank you very much. You may stand down and you're excused from further attending court.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Black?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next witness will be called by my colleague, Ms. Anna Richterova. We'll just switch places with him and then she will proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, I haven't introduced myself officially yet. My name is Anna Richterova. I am a new member of the Prosecution team. And I would like to call the next Prosecution witness, Radoslav Maksic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much Mr. -- Ms. Richterova.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the witness please make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Maksic. You may proceed, Ms. Richterova.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Maksic. Could you please state your full name for the record?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: Radoslav Maksic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: With the Court's permission I would like to read the background information which are not I assume in any dispute. You were born on 27 of August 1939 in Grbice, Kragujevac?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: You attended military academy, command staff academy, and the national defence school?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: In 1981, you were the class head at the military academy?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: From 1985 to 1987, you were the head of the training section in the department for operations and training in the staff of the Belgrade corps?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Between 1987 and 1988, you held the same position in the operational section of the department for operations and training in the staff of Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Between 1989 and 1993, you were the chief of the department for operations and training in the staff of the Belgrade corps?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Mr. Maksic, in the second half of 1991, did you receive some other assignment outside of Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can you tell us, can you tell the Court, what was it?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: In late September 1991, I went to Krajina as chief of the operations department of the Krajina TO staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: May I show the witness the document, 65 ter number is 1233. Do you have this document in front of you on the screen?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: This document is dated 20th of September 1991, and was issued by the Federal Secretariat for National Defence. Can you tell us what this document is about?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: It's not dated the 28th of September but, rather, the 20th of September.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yeah, it must have been wrongly translated because I stated 20th of September.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can you please state what this document is about?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: This document states that among others, I am sent over to the Territorial Defence staff of the Serbian autonomous district of Krajina, to the Knin garrison.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can we scroll down a little bit the document? Can you see on this page other people who were assigned to go to the Krajina region?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Who was it?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: Colonel Kasum, Dusan, son of Obrad. Colonel Maksic, that's me. Colonel Milos Pupovac.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can we please go to the second page?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: Lieutenant Colonel Aleksandar Vuletic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: We can see that there are more names. How many people altogether went to Krajina?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: In this first order, only three persons went pursuant to this first order.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit number 120, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Mr. Maksic, before September, when you received the document about your new assignment, did you talk to someone from Krajina regarding this new assignment?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Who do you speak -- who did you speak?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: In late June or early July, I talked to president of Krajina, Milan Babic, who asked me to come to Krajina in order to organise the TO Defence units of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: What was your initial reaction to this?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: Initially I refused to go. However, subsequently I changed my mind and accepted to go to Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: What made you change your mind?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: I was in service in a unit which had 70 or 80 per cent of the Territorial Defence men, and I was known as some kind of an expert for Territorial Defence issues. Therefore, I wanted to help to organise the Territorial Defence of Krajina, which, according to Babic's words, was split and disorganised.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: When you say it was split, split between what?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: Well, the Territorial Defence was organised via units, squads, platoons, and companies. However, when the 9th Corps was mobilised as well as the police forces, manpower from these units went into those units. Therefore, the Territorial Defence did not exist as an institution. There were only staffs and there were some elderly people who were not fit for military purposes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: According to the law, could you be transferred to this position in a different republic?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: In accordance with the then-law, it was possible. However, it was an exception. Commanders of territorial staffs and in the republics and in provinces, in this case we had such a commander in Krajina, all of these people were active-duty officers.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I would like to show the witness 65 ter Exhibit 155.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Do you have this document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could we have the English version of it, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: This decision is dated 30th of September 1991 and it is decision on appointing of Lieutenant Colonel Ilija Djujic to the position of commander of the Serb autonomous region of Krajina Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: I can just see the preamble, not the text itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Would you be so kind, please, and scroll down a little bit with the document? Can you see it now?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Is it correct that he was appointed to this position?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Do you know the reason why Ilija Djujic was appointed to this position?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: Ilija Djujic hailed from Knin. He was a general in the former JNA, Lieutenant General. He was quite a prominent person. At that point he was retired and it was believed that he was the one who could do the most in order to organise the Territorial Defence of the SAO Krajina. It was believed so because he knew both the people there and the territory.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit number 121, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to show the witness a document, 65 ter 154. Can we scroll down this document a little bit?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: This document doesn't bear any number. However, as you can see, it states the various positions of people who were supposed to be members of this staff. Can you please read -- do you please agree that the positions as stated in this document, these people really held?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: That's precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And according to this document, you were appointed as the head of the operative educational department?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can you -- just briefly stated, what were the tasks of the commander of the staff? The primary tasks?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: Commander was in charge of the staff, or rather the TO units, through the TO staff of Krajina. He also planned combat operations, was in charge of mobilisation, training, logistics, and all other issues which contribute to combat readiness of a unit. He did this via his organs or departments. He also maintained communication with various institutions, such as president of the republic, commander of the 9th Corps, Minister of the Interior, and other organs which had an impact on the preparation and organisation of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And you, as the head of the operative educational department, what were your tasks?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: Commander of the unit for operations and training organised, planned, carried out and monitored training, planned combat operations, potential combat operations, and proposed them to the commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit number 122, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Before I start with another document, I think it's the time for a break so we don't stop in the middle of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. If it is then convenient to take a break at this stage we will do so. Court will adjourn and we'll come back at quarter to 11. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Richterova.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Witness, before we start talking about the activities of TO and your role in the staff, I would like you to explain the Judges the structure of TO. When you gave the statement, you also prepared a chart, and I would like -- I would like the usher to show you the chart, and I have copies for the Judges and the Defence. I have to apologise because this chart hasn't been translated yet but it's being translated. We will have it very soon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can we place it on the ELMO? That's perfect, like this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Your Honours, do you have it on your screens?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No, not on my screen. Yeah, we now have it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Because we do not have the translation, can you please slowly read and indicate on the hard copy what are you reading? First of all, do you recognise it as a chart which you prepared?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can you tell us what exactly we can see on this chart?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: It says here, "Organisational Chart of the TO Staff in Krajina, the 1st of September 1991," and then the following, "Ministry of Defence of Serbia assists and organises the establishment of the Krajina TO Staff via the Serbian Republic of Krajina." This staff is composed of zone staffs. One such staff being in Banija, the next one in Lika, and the third one in Kordun. These zone staffs had all municipalities subordinated to them and consequently municipal staffs were subordinated to them as well. Here on the chart, you cannot see that Banija and Kordun or the second and third zone were merged into one staff. Zone staff for Lika and Northern Dalmatia was a single structure. On the other hand, the Ministry of Interior of Serbia, or rather the Ministry of Police of Krajina were linked to the Ministry of the Interior of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: When you said that a Ministry of Interior of Krajina was linked to Ministry of Interior of Serbia, what do you base this statement on?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: I base it on the technical assistance that it received from the Ministry of Interior of Serbia, the assistance provided to the police of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What you did want to say, Ms. Richterova, is that the witness said the Ministry of Police of Krajina is linked to the Ministry of Interior of Serbia, not the two interior ministries. You said the Ministry of Interior of Krajina was linked to the Ministry of Interior of Serbia but here it said the Ministry of Police of Krajina was linked to the Ministry of the Interior of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can the witness just clarify that point, which is which, what is linked to what?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Mr. Maksic, can you please clarify what is the correct statement?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: It's the same thing. I just used a different term. Ministry of the Interior of Krajina was linked to the Ministry of the Interior of Serbia. In my chart I put down Ministry of Police. It should read Ministry of the Interior. It's the same thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I would like this document to be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document will be admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit number 123, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: To continue with the structure of the TO, I would like to show the witness another document. It is 65 ter number 1854. Your Honours, do you have English version on your screens?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No. We now have an English version. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: This document is from the 3rd of October 1991. Can we go to the paragraph 2?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Maksic, can you read what is stated in paragraph 2?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: "Pursuant to the order of the Prime Minister of SAO Krajina, active Colonel of the JNA Vujaklija, Rade is hereby appointed commander of the 2nd and 3rd operative zone for Banija and Kordun whereas Tarbuk Milan is hereby appointed Chief of Staff." Tarbuk Milan is a retired Lieutenant Colonel.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Does it reflect correctly the situation when you were in Krajina?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: Whether item 2 is correct? Yes, pursuant to the order, Rade Vujaklija, active duty JNA colonel, was appointed commander of the operational zone for Banija and Kordun and in fact Milan Tarbuk was also appointed, and I believe it was in early December that he assumed the position of the Minister of Defence of Krajina. As for this document, this is a circular, and the -- its purpose was to inform all the municipal TO staffs of these appointments to the Republic TO Staff. This one in particular pertains to the Glina municipality, as far as I remember, and all the TO commanders and presidents of municipalities received this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: This document says that 2nd and 3rd Operative Zone, which was for Banija and Kordun, had one commander. What about the 1st zone?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: The 1st zone, that one being Dalmatia and Lika zone had the TO staff which was at the same time the staff of the zone itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: So can you tell us --

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: The two zones, that's to say.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can you tell us who was the commander of this 1st Operative Zone?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: The commander of the 1st operations zone was the Krajina TO Staff Commander, General Ilija Djujic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: If we can move to the paragraph 3, first sentence, and it says "a stand was taken at the level of the SAO Krajina government" --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milovancevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I have an objection. I believe that my learned friend Prosecutor should allow the witness to see what is contained in the document. That's to say to quote from the document. And then let the witness make his conclusions. She should take it the other way around.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Ms. Richterova?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I can do it this way as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Mr. Maksic, please can you read the first paragraph -- the first sentence of the third paragraph?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: "At the level of the SAO Krajina government, therefore, on the level of the government, not the staff, the position was taken to the effect that the SAO Krajina Prime Minister should appoint the commander and the Chief of Staff of the TO municipalities and commanders of TO units with his order, which is in accordance with the standard procedure in the army, because the SAO Krajina Prime Minister appoints commanders of zone TO staffs and these in turn appoint commanders of municipal TO staffs. Therefore, this particular provision here is contrary to the standard procedure in the army.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Mr. Maksic, to your knowledge, was this procedure implemented?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: This was not implemented.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit number 124, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I would like to show the witness document 65 ter number 193. Can we scroll down, please? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: This document is dated 14 of November 1991. Can you please have a look at the document and tell the Court what this document is about?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: Sava Radulovic, reserve major, was commander of the TO staff in Knin. He was relieved of his duty because of his age, and was transferred to the Republic TO Staff of Krajina as an administrative officer. He was replaced by a person whose name I cannot recall. I believe he was a gym teacher.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Mr. Maksic, can you tell us who signed this decision and please can you scroll down?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: It was signed by Prime Minister Milan Babic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And as you stated, he was a commander of municipality Territorial Defence, is it correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: The municipal Territorial Defence in Knin. Since at the time Babic was president of Knin municipality, it was within his competence to do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit number 125, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Just for completion I would like to show the witness document 65 ter number 194. Can you please scroll down?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: This document is dated 14 of November 1991. Can you please tell the Judges what this document is about?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: This document reads that Slavko Ozegovic is appointed commander instead of Slavko -- I don't remember his family name. So he is appointed commander of the Territorial Defence of Knin municipality. This again is in accordance with the regulations in force at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: You can see, Your Honours, that the translation wrongly stated the name of this person as "Okegovic" instead of Ozegovic. We will request a revision of this translation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ozegovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: How is Ozegovic spelt?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] O-Z-E-G-O-V-I-C.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Was Milan Babic authorised to replace a commander of municipality Territorial Defence from other municipality other than Knin?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: At the time, Milan Babic was also president of the Republic of Serbian Krajina and president of Knin municipality. Therefore, he was in a position to do that. At the same time, he had the power to remove other commanders of Territorial Defence of other municipalities in agreement with the presidents of the respective municipalities who were also commanders.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit number 126, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I have one more document which I would like to show the witness, and it is 65 ter number 1239.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: This document is dated 5th of October 1991. Can you please read the heading of this document?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: "To municipal staffs of Territorial Defence and Municipal Secretariats for National Defence of Gracac, Donji Lapac and Korenica."

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Now I would like you to read the first sentence of this document.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: "According to our information, in the areas of your municipalities, there is an initiative" - I'm not sure, I cannot read this word - "for the establishment of a special operative zone for the Territorial Defence in your municipalities. Based on this we wish to inform you that pursuant to a directive of the Prime Minister of the Serbian Autonomous District of Krajina, number" - I can't make it - "of the 10th of August 1991, the operations zones were set up of the Territorial Defence of the SAO Krajina, namely, first zone, Dalmatia-Lika, for the municipalities of Knin, Benkovac, Obrovac, Gracac, Donji Lapac and Korenica. Second, Kordun for the municipalities of Vojcic, Vrgin Most and Slunj, and the third Banija for the municipalities of Dvor on the Una, Glina, Kostajnica, Petrinja, and Sisak. I would like to -- the document to be scrolled up a bit so I can see who signed the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can we scroll it down? Can you read who signed this document?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was signed by Milan Babic as the person responsible. Can we scroll the document up again to the beginning, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can you scroll it up, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can you explain to the Judges the significance --

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Thank you. You see, nowhere in the text does it say who launched such an initiative. This is Milan Babic's reply but one cannot make out who it is addressed to or, rather, who launched the initiative, whether some of the presidents here or a third party.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Mr. Maksic, this document is addressed to the municipal staffs of these three municipalities, Gracac, Donji Lapac and Korenica?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: To your knowledge, is -- does this document reflect the situation as it was?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: No. I've seen this document recently. There was no reason why these three municipalities should be singled out as a separate zone within a zone, because they were already part of a zone. Knin, Benkovac, Gracac and Donji Lapac, these municipalities were part of the Dalmatia-Lika zone. So now, as part of Dalmatia-Lika zone based on someone's request - we don't know who put forth such a request - they are to form part of a new zone.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Mr. Maksic, based to your knowledge of the situation in Krajina at the time you were there, what was the purpose of this letter?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: I can only conclude that, and I don't have any firm base for that, the municipalities in Banija, Lika, Kordun and northern Dalmatia, and I'm not sure which ones in particular, were divided. Some favoured Milan Martic, others favoured Milan Babic. One of them enjoyed greater support in some municipalities, the other in others. There could have been no other reason, from a military perspective, to establish a separate zone within a zone.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: When you said that some municipalities favoured Milan Martic, others favoured Milan Babic, can you explain what exactly you mean?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: I mean by that that some municipalities supported Mr. Martic's concept about how the TO and the Krajina army were to be organised, whereas others -- other municipalities supported Mr. Babic's concept on the same matter. That's to say there were two concepts there. First, that the Ministry of the Interior should be competent for the entire police force and the army in Krajina, whereas Babic advocated following idea, that the police and the army should be separate entities, each performing their own tasks, which was normally the case. And that was the gist of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: To your knowledge, do you know which concept materialised?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: Out of these two concepts, and this is something one can deduce at a later stage, after the withdrawal of the 9th corps, that Milan Babic's concept prevailed because the TO units which were left behind after the withdrawal and were properly [Realtime transcript read in error "probably"] organised were separate from the Ministry of the Interior, although they had similar tasks. Still, they had separate commands and cooperated along the principles along which a Ministry of the Interior and an army usually cooperate. The same -- there was an attempt to do the same thing in Serbia in 1992 and 1993, that the Ministry of the Interior should take over the powers of the army and the army would be given some peripheral tasks.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Mr. Maksic, you stated now, after the withdrawal and were probably -- I'm sorry, "Babic's concept prevailed because the TO units which were left behind after the withdrawal and were probably organised" - doesn't make too much sense - "were separate from the Ministry of the Interior." What do you mean that TO was separated from the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: Perhaps I haven't made myself clear. The TO and the Ministry of the Interior of Krajina were never a joint body. They never had a joint command. However, there was this idea to unite the two into a single armed force.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And whose idea it was?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: I don't know whose idea it was but there was an attempt to realise the idea through the Ministry of the Interior. The setting up of the municipal TO staffs and the units which were supposed to make part of the staff, and these were manoeuvre units active throughout the territory of Krajina, was not advocated by anyone. The 9th Corps and the -- and General Djujic and the Minister of the Interior all obstructed this idea. First of all, they didn't want a TO staff to be set up. What was in place was not even a staff up until December 1991, because it numbered four members, and they did not have a single TO unit. They tried to establish some units like in Benkovac, a brigade, a battalion in Kistanje which was there from before. Then there was some units at the strength of a company but they were all automatically resubordinated to the 9th Corps which commanded over them. Therefore, the staff did not have a single unit, not even of the smallest strength, not even a single courier.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: We will talk about this a little bit later. I would like to finish with this particular document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can we scroll down to the last paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And please, Mr. Maksic, can you read the last paragraph of this document?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: "Hereby we wish -- I wish to inform you that as technical organs, you should caution those responsible that all the activities and setting up zone and municipal TO staffs must be in accordance with the regulations of the Serbian Autonomous District of Krajina and that all your suggestions on these activities should be addressed to the commander of the TO of the SAO Krajina, Lieutenant General Djujic, Ilija." I was kept abreast of the events at the time. We did not receive a single suggestion to that effect. Perhaps General Djujic did. But we were never shown anything of the sort, Kasum and I. And I was there until the 27th of December and none of this materialised. There is this one question that comes to my mind: Who was behind all of this? And who is Mr. Babic sending this answer or this reply to? Whether it's to the presidents of municipalities or -- please, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Maksic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we do that, can I just ask a question? Mr. Maksic, I noticed that this document is said to be signed by the president, Mr. Milan Babic. The prior two or three documents that we have -- that have been tendered in so far, he is titled, "Prime Minister." Does this make any difference?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. It's the same thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. The document will then be admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit number 127, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Your Honours, meanwhile, we received the translation of that chart. I would like to distribute it and include it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the English version of the chart please be admitted into evidence and be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit number 128, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Mr. Maksic, you stated that the creation of the staff was obstructed, you were not able to -- you didn't have enough manpower. To your knowledge, what was the purpose of creating of this staff, this Main Staff of the TO?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: I suppose that the establishment of the TO staff of SAO Krajina sometime in September or in October was supposed to represent a preparatory step for accepting the units of the 9th Corps, once the 9th Corps relocated from that area, because most of the members of the 9th Corps of the JNA had been mobilised from that area. Those people were supposed to remain in that territory and that staff was supposed to recreate those units to turn them, transform them, into new units and to create a new structure and so on. Then there was another aspect, which I came to realise only later, which is that Milan Babic was supposed to counterbalance Mr. Martic. I think that this thesis is quite a reasonable one. Mr. Martic had armed men under his command. He had policemen, whereas Babic had only political power in his hands. Usually the one who has arms and weapons under his command is the actual authority. Therefore, Babic wanted to threaten Mr. Martic, telling him that he would create an army of his own. It was my impression that Babic did that in order to spite Martic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Mr. Maksic, what was the position of Milan Babic in relation to the Main Staff of the TO, or better say the authority of Milan Babic?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: He was the Supreme Commander of the TO staff, as a Prime Minister of Serbian Autonomous Region of Krajina and he was the only one authorised to issue orders to the TO staff. It existed only on paper and it had only three or four of us as its staff members, without any units.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Did you receive any orders from Mr. Babic?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: We received orders in principle from Mr. Babic to establish units of the Territorial Defence. However, he didn't provide any terms and conditions for us in order to do that. We had no financial or any other resources to establish these units. Whatever was fit for military service, whoever was fit for military service, went to serve either in the Ministry of the Interior or in the 9th Corps of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Mr. Maksic, I would like to briefly talk about the relationship between the SAO Krajina TO and the Ministry of Defence of Republic of Serbia. Was there any relationship?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: I did not understand your question. Would you please repeat it?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Was there any relationship between Main Staff of SAO Krajina and Ministry of Defence of Republika of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Serbia had a general who served as a coordinator. That was General Kuzmanovic. He was in charge of coordinating the work of the TO Krajina Staff and the Ministry of Defence. He was replaced later on by General Djordjevic. We communicated exclusively through him and very seldom at that. We mostly sent requests for materiel supplies, communications equipment, other types of equipment, weapons, and so on. We sent requests. These requests should still exist somewhere in the archives in their written form. They were sent as early as August. I think that during that time, Mr. Banatic [phoen] was Defence Minister. I'm not so sure about that. These requests were later repeated but we received nothing that was requested by us. I can't say nothing, because we received several telephones, maybe five telephones, including field telephones, but they were quite outdated and practically unusable. This is how it was up until the 27th of December 1991. I don't know what happened afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Mr. Maksic, I would like to show you a document, 65 ter number 1283. And under this number, there are, in fact, three documents. I would like to show only document which bears in B/C/S ERN number 02076715. This document is dated 16 of December 1991. Can you have a look at this document and tell us to whom this document was addressed?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: It was sent to the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Serbia. They are asking for reinforcements of staff units. This is a request for receiving such reinforcements.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Mr. Maksic, is this an example of request for equipments?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was preparing to leave on the 16th of December. That was in 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can we --

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: At that time -- may I continue?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yes, please. I only want to scroll down this document, for you to see who signed this document.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: It was signed by Colonel Milos Pupovac. He came, I don't know what date it was, I don't know whether he came a day or two earlier or perhaps even three days, and he immediately sent a request for this equipment, for replenishment, asking for the equipment listed in this document. I told you that this request was sent back in August, perhaps even July, if I'm not mistaken, when Mr. Martic was Defence Minister. And such requests were simply copied down and resent. However, this has to do with something else. They are sending a request here to replenish staff units which in fact did not exist at all. At this point in time, on the 16th of December, there was not a single unit within the TO Staff. They existed only on paper. There were plans to establish units under such and such circumstances, and this equipment was needed for these units. There is also another explanation possible, that the 9th Corps, after leaving the area, it was supposed to leave the area, resubordinated this or left it to these units. So this is not clear to me at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Mr. Maksic, you mentioned that you didn't receive anything. Who was responsible to equip these local TO units?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: Local TO units were supposed to be equipped by municipalities, rather the presidents of municipalities. There were local units and manoeuvre units. Let me give you a brief explanation. Territorial units are linked to the territory of a municipality and if there are any combat operations to be carried out, they can be carried out only in the territory of that municipality. Municipalities purchased equipment and weapons using their own funds. In addition to these units, there were also manoeuvre units which were larger units, size of battalion or brigade. They were intended to act in the entire territory of Banija Lika, Kordun, and Northern Dalmatia or, for example, Serbia. There existed such units in Serbia as well. So the territorial units, which are municipal units as we used to call them, were supposed to be equipped and armed by presidents of municipalities. As for the manoeuvre units, which were larger units, they were supposed to be equipped by the government of the Republic of Krajina or rather the president of Krajina via the TO staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Mr. Maksic, all these TO units which join 9th Corps, were they all equipped with weapons, ammunition, everything what they needed?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: I don't remember the date but I think that in early 1991, in the entire territory of then still unified Yugoslavia, an order was issued stipulating that all equipment, all weapons in the depots of Territorial Defence was supposed to be transferred to the JNA. JNA was given jurisdiction so to speak over that equipment. So whatever they had was now in the possession of the JNA. However, it is true that all territorial units which were organised in the form of platoons and so on had their weapons and equipment. Those which did not have an assignment did not have weapons and equipment. When the mobilisation of the 9th Corps was carried out, a large number of these TO units became a component of the 9th Corps because there was simply not enough men. Therefore, some TO units ceased to exist because they joined battalions, platoons, companies, of the 9th Corps. They were mobilised into them and, in such way, transformed. Those which did not join the 9th corps became Territorial Defence units based on the capabilities of a municipality. If a municipality was a small one, it had a small unit. If it was a large one, it had a large unit. Some TO units became units of the Ministry of the Interior and then whatever was left was used to establish Territorial Defence units, and as I said it depended on the resources in a municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Mr. Maksic, I will stop you here. You said some TO units became units of the Ministry of the Interior. Can you explain this a little bit further? How did they become units of the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: You see, in 1991, the mobilisation system which was known until then ceased to exist in the territory of Krajina. The 9th Corps was not a Serbian corps; within the 9th Corps, there were Croats serving there. They went wherever they went. And then all of a sudden, I don't know the exact percentage, 10, 20, 30 per cent or something along those lines, was missing. That was the percentage of personnel missing. In order to bring up the numbers to the establishment strength, they had to mobilise people who were present in that territory and those were people of Serb ethnicity. Once those units, certain units, were disbanded in order to reinforce the JNA units, some people wanted to join police units and some wanted to join the JNA units.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Not to forget, I would like to tender the document which we were talking about into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is tendered -- is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit number 129, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Mr. Maksic, you mentioned at the beginning of your testimony, when I asked you about your tasks, that your tasks were planned, carried out, and monitored trainings, plan combat operations, potential combat operations, and propose them to the commander.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I would like to talk now a little bit about the relationship between the TO and the 9th Corps. The 9th Corps was the unit which operated on which territory?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: The 9th corps was in charge of all combat operations in the territory of Northern Dalmatia, Lika, but mostly Northern Dalmatia.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I would like to show the witness a document 65 ter number 2053. This document is dated 26 of October 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can you please read the first -- the heading or the initial part of this, above order? Above the order? Yeah.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV MAKSIC
utterances.text: "Lately, certain commands following the mobilisation and completed preparations of certain war units are moving those units at their own initiative. They are relocating and resubordinating these units. In order to ensure efficient command and control, as well as rational and planned use of units, I hereby order." Shall I read on?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And please read the order number 1.
